To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Raa1, Raa2, and Raa3 are components of a multiprotein complex that is required for chloroplast group II RNA splicing.
the nuclear genes Raa1, Raa2, and Raa3 are required for trans-splicing of the psaAB operon.
the Raa1 and 2 proteins are associated in a multiprotein complex of 400 to 500 kD that is involved in chloroplast intron splicing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the multiprotein complex that catalyzes group II intron trans-splicing in the chloroplast of the alga Chlamydoponas.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are part of a complex involved in chloroplastic group II intron trans-splicing.
the identification and characterization of proteins required for chloroplast group II splicing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the splicing of the psa A gene is mediated by a complex of at least 14 nuclear and 1 chloroplastic factors.
the Raa complex is involved in splicing of the psa A gene.
the Raa1-Raa2 complex represents the minimal functional unit required for splicing of the group II intron of the psaB gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Raa1-Raa2 complex is involved in the second trans-spliciug reaction and is part of a multiprotein complex of 400 to 500 kD.
the splicing of psaA introns is mediated by a multiprotein complex, the integrity of which is affected by mutations in several different complementation groups.
Raa1-Raa2 and Raa3 are components of two different complexes involved in trans-splicing of the psa gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trans-splicing of group II introns requires a complex of proteins that may be similar to the spliceosome in its composition and function.
group II intron trans-splicing requires a multiprotein complex, and that this complex is involved in more than one trans-splicing step.
the trans-splicing of the psa A gene in Chlamydomonadaceae is mediated by a large multiprotein complex.
